The registry core and the first eight widgets are unchanged; the new eight are added below them.

## 1. `HRL_INTERACTIVE.names()` — all sixteen

`names()` walks the registry and returns a sorted list. These sixteen are registered:

`armCareCheck`, `assignTheNine`, `countBuilder`, `gradeTheTool`, `labelTheField`, `makeTheCall`, `placeThePositions`, `runnerAdvance`, `safeOrOut`, `scoreThePlay`, `sequencePitches`, `spotTheAlignment`, `statMatch`, `stealRead`, `strikeZoneTrainer`, `swingOrder`

(I did not execute `names()` — no shell this turn. Confirmation is from the sixteen `register(...)` calls at the bottom of the file.)

---

## 2. New widgets — opts, missing fields, keyboard

Shared: `question` → `prompt` → `text` → `description`, then a string `situation` if needed. `resolveAnswerIndex` treats a numeric `answer` as a `choices` index and a string as choice text. Empty/malformed `opts` render `.empty-state` and return. Every widget has **Check**, **Reset**, and `.widget-status` (`aria-live="polite"`). Second miss reveals the answer.

### `assignTheNine`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `prompt`/`situation`, `correct` (`p`/`c`/`1b`/`2b`/`3b`/`ss`/`lf`/`cf`/`rf` → `ball`|`base`|`backup`), `rationale`, `diagram.{svg,opts}`.
**Missing:** no usable cases (or no `correct` roles) → empty-state. Missing `diagram` still draws a field from `situation`. Missing `prompt` is built from `situation`.
**Keyboard:** tab the Ball/Base/Backup palette or the three role buttons on each of the nine rows; Enter/Space assigns. Field hotspots are `role="button"` with the same keys. **Show the answer** appears after a miss. Running score is jobs out of 9×cases, plus perfect-situation count; Next/Finish walks the set.

### `stealRead`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `description`/`prompt`, `move`, `answer` (`go`|`hold`|`balk`), `explain`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. Unknown `move` still shows a generic foot-direction diagram.
**Keyboard:** Tab to Go / Hold / Balk (`.choice-btn`), Enter/Space to pick, then Check. SVG foot animation is omitted when `ctx.reducedMotion()` is true.

### `makeTheCall`
**Reads:** `mode` (label only), `cases[]` with `prompt`/`situation`/`question`, `choices[]`, `answer` (index **or** text), `explain`, optional `rule`, `division`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. Empty `choices` shows a hint, Check stays inert until a pick exists. Unknown `mode` uses the default “Make the call” copy and does not throw.
**Keyboard:** Tab through `.choice-btn` rulings, Enter/Space to select, Check. After resolve, `rule` / `division` are announced when present.

### `sequencePitches`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `hitter`, `count`, `pitches[{type,location,x,y,call}]`, `ideal[{type,location}]`, `explain`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. Missing `ideal` grades only the learner’s own eye-level/speed flags.
**Keyboard:** Tab available pitch tokens, Enter/Space to add (max 3); Tab to **Remove** on a slot. Check grades **principles** (eye level / speed, compared with what the ideal actually does) — not an exact match.

### `scoreThePlay`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `description`, `answer`, `accept[]`, `explain`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. Empty `accept` still matches `answer`.
**Keyboard:** 1–9, E, FC, K, ꓘ, F, U, hyphen, and **Delete last** are real buttons; the text field is typed/pasteable (Enter submits Check). Comparison folds case, whitespace, “backward(s) K” / “K-looking” → ꓘ.

### `statMatch`
**Reads:** `pairs[{stat,question,hides}]`, optional `traps[{question,lure,explain}]`.
**Missing:** no valid pairs → empty-state. `traps` omitted → questions column is pairs only.
**Keyboard:** Tab statistic buttons, then question buttons; Enter/Space selects. A second selection tries the pair. Wrong trap questions use `traps[].explain`. A correct match surfaces `hides`. Check reveals leftovers on a second miss.

### `gradeTheTool`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `tool`, `description`, `grade`, `tolerance` (default **5**), `explain`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. Non-numeric `grade` treated as 50; missing `tolerance` → 5.
**Keyboard:** **−5** / **+5** buttons (step 5, clamped 20–80) and a `type="range"` slider (arrow keys). Gauge is `HRL_SVG.scaleGauge`. Copy on screen: 50 is major-league average.

### `spotTheAlignment`
**Reads:** `cases[]` with `situation`, `options[]` (ids), `answer` (id **or** index), `preview`, `explain`.
**Missing:** no cases → empty-state. `preview` falsy → name buttons only.
**Keyboard:** Tab `.choice-btn` (each preview field is inside the button), Enter/Space to pick, Check.

---

## 3. Curriculum `opts` vs this brief (followed the data)

| Widget | What the files actually pass | How it was handled |
|---|---|---|
| **`assignTheNine`** | `prompt` plus `diagram: { svg:'field', opts:{ positions, alignment, ball, runners, title } }`, not just `situation` | Situation line prefers `prompt`. Diagram opts are copied into `HRL_SVG.field`; `roles` and `hotspots` are added at draw time. |
| **`stealRead`** | `move` is an id (`rhp-home`, `rhp-pickoff-first`, `lhp-crosses-45`, `no-stop`, …), not a diagram object. Field is `explain`, not a separate tell | Mapped those ids to a pitcher-foot SVG + `basePaths` (runner at first; first-and-third for `fake-to-third`). `explain` is the tell. |
| **`makeTheCall`** | `answer` is usually a **number index** (ch04, ch08, ch16, ch17, ch19, ch20, ch24). Modes: `safety`, `game-flow`, `small-ball`, `rules`, `approach`, `management`. Also used in **ch19**, not only 4/8/16/17/20/24. Both `prompt` and `situation` often present | Shared index-or-text helper. `mode` is only a labelling hint; unknown modes use the default. `promptOrSituation` never prints `undefined`. |
| **`sequencePitches`** | `pitches` are **objects** `{type, location, x, y, call}`, not strings. `ideal` is `{type, location}` ×3 | Buttons from those objects; zone plots `x`/`y` with numbered pitches. Exact type+location match is a bonus, not required. |
| **`scoreThePlay`** | `accept` includes `643`, `DP 6-4-3`, `1B`/`single`, `ꓘ`/`Kc`/`backward K`, etc. | Builder **and** typed input; fold then match `answer` plus every `accept`. |
| **`statMatch`** | `traps: [{ question, lure, explain }]` — lure is a stat name used as a distractor question | Trap questions are shuffled into the question column. Pairing one is always wrong and shows `explain`. `lure` is not a second correct key. |
| **`gradeTheTool`** | Matches the brief (`grade`, `tolerance: 5` on every case) | Default tolerance 5 if omitted. |
| **`spotTheAlignment`** | `answer` is an **id string** (`standard`, `infield-in`, …). `preview: true` on all 8 cases. Curriculum only uses it in **ch13**, not ch16 | Options rendered as ids; labels mapped (`dp-depth` → “Double-play depth”). `preview` draws a small `field` per option. |
| **Shared** | Extra fields (`id`, `source`, `prompt` vs `question`) | Read defensively; never rendered as `undefined`. |

`sequencePitches` grading vs exact match: a sequence is counted correct if it matches the ideal line **or** it makes the same principle moves the ideal makes (change eye level if the ideal does; change speeds if the ideal does). The 0–2 “late on the fastball” ideal is all fastballs, so staying on the heater still passes. Status text always says more than one good sequence exists.

---

## 4. CSS classes not already in `styles.css`

None. New markup uses existing classes: `.choice-btn` (+ `.selected` / `.correct` / `.wrong`), `.token`, `.dropzone`, `.btn` / `.btn-sm` / `.btn-primary` / `.btn-ghost` / `.btn-accent`, `.hint`, `.quiz-explain`, `.progress-bar` / `.progress-bar-fill`, `.empty-state`, `.widget-status`, `.widget-actions`, `.hrl-svg`. Layout that those classes do not cover is inline styles, same as the first eight widgets.

---

## 5. Deviations (and why)

- **`assignTheNine` “Show the answer”** is offered after the **first** miss as well as auto-revealed on the second, so the learner is never stuck. The brief said “after a second attempt.”
- **`sequencePitches`** does not require an exact `ideal` match (brief + chapter intro both say not to). A 3–1 sequence that changes speed when the ideal stayed on the fastball can still pass if eye level changes; the authored `explain` still teaches “don’t throw the changeup you cannot throw for a strike.”
- **`statMatch`** auto-pairs on the second click (stat then question) instead of waiting for Check. Check still scores / reveals. Matches how “select a, then select b” is supposed to feel.
- **`stealRead` animation** is a small custom SVG (rubber, plate, 1B/3B, free-foot motion), not a clip in `HRL_SVG`. Known `move` ids from ch15 are mapped; reduced motion draws the end pose only.
- **`gradeTheTool` first miss** does **not** draw the compare marker on the gauge (that would leak the answer). Distance (“off by 15”) is announced instead.
- **`spotTheAlignment`** is implemented for every alignment id `HRL_SVG.field` already knows, including ch16 if it is wired later; the current curriculum only mounts it in ch13.

No TODOs, no stub `mount`s, no rewrite of the first eight widgets.
